candidates.exact_span: 7. The permittee shall prepare annually a list of Industrial Users which during the preceding twelve months were in significant noncompliance with applicable pretreatment requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this annual list-preparation obligation applies to the evaluated period, and whether evidence of its performance is required, depends on interpreting 'annually' and 'preceding twelve months' relative to Federal FY2025 and on whether evaluated entities are Industrial Users subject to this Part.

candidates.exact_span: For the purposes of this Part, significant noncompliance shall be determined based upon the more stringent of either criteria established at 40 CFR Part 403.8(f)(2)(viii) [rev. 10/14/05] or criteria established in the approved POTW pretreatment program.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of which criteria are 'more stringent,' or what the approved POTW pretreatment program criteria are, could change whether an Industrial User is classified as in significant noncompliance and therefore whether related reporting obligations were triggered.

candidates.exact_span: This list is to be published annually in a newspaper of general circulation that provides meaningful public notice within the jurisdiction(s) served by the POTW during the month of January.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the January publication deadline and what satisfies 'meaningful public notice' could change whether a separate public-notice monitoring/reporting requirement was applicable for FY2025 and whether available evidence establishes compliance with that obligation.

candidates.exact_span: In addition, during the month of January the permittee shall submit an updated pretreatment program status report to EPA and the State containing the following information:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this January status-report submission was required in FY2025 affects monitoring-obligation evaluation (Purpose B). If no report is present, interpretation of this requirement also affects whether the absence is a documented no-data state, required monitoring/reporting lacking evidence, or unresolved (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: An updated list of all significant industrial users and identify which Industrial Users are Non-Significant Categorical Industrial Users (NSCIUs) or Middle Tier CIUs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification as a significant industrial user, NSCIU, or Middle Tier CIU can change which pretreatment monitoring and reporting requirements are actually applicable under referenced federal frameworks, so different readings of these categories could change evaluated obligation sets.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to categorical Pretreatment Standards that are subject to reduced monitoring and reporting requirements under 40 CFR 403.12(e)(2) & (3);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an Industrial User falls within reduced monitoring under 403.12(e)(2) and (3) can change which monitoring is required (B), whether numeric compliance comparisons are applicable versus report-only obligations (A), and whether missing results reflect conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to the following categorical Pretreatment Standards [Organic Chemicals, Plastics, and Synthetic Fibers (OCPSF) (40 CFR part 414), Petroleum Refining (40 CFR part 419), and Pesticide Chemicals (40 CFR part 455)] and for which the Control Authority has chosen to use the concentration-based standards rather than converting them to flow-based mass standards as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(6);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the Control Authority chose concentration-based rather than flow-based mass standards determines which enforceable numeric limit form applies to reported measurements for covered categorical Industrial Users, changing limit-applicability and exceedance computations.

candidates.exact_span: Categorical Industrial Users subject to concentration-based standards for which the Control Authority has chosen to convert the concentration-based standards to equivalent mass limits, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(5);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether equivalent mass limits were elected under 403.6(c)(5) changes the applicable enforceable numeric limit used to compare reported discharge measurements against categorical pretreatment standards.

candidates.exact_span: General Control Mechanisms used for similar groups of SIUs along with the substantially similar types of operations and the types of wastes that are the same, for each separate General Control Mechanism, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.8(f)(1)(iii);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether a General Control Mechanism applies to a given group of SIUs, and whether operations and wastes are 'substantially similar' and 'the same,' could change the operative limits and monitoring/reporting framework applied to grouped users rather than individual limits.
